titulo: The present to tell past events
regla: Spanish often tells past events in the present tense: in history and biographies (presente histórico), in news headlines, and in lively everyday stories (Ayer voy por la calle y me encuentro a Juan). It makes the past feel close and vivid.

lista.texto: **Hidalgo da el Grito de Dolores en 1810.** Very common in textbooks and timelines.
**Rescatan a dos excursionistas en el Nevado de Toluca.** The event feels fresh.
**Ayer voy saliendo del metro y ¿a quién me encuentro?** It drops the listener into the scene.

bloques.texto: A date or time phrase (**en 1810, ayer, el sábado**) usually makes clear it's the past.
In conversation, people mix it with the preterite to highlight the key moment.
Tip: the present tense is a time machine: it takes the listener back with you.

lista.es: El 15 de abril de 1912 ==se hunde== el Titanic.

lista.en: Frida Kahlo was born in Coyoacán in 1907.

lista.es: ==Descubren== una ciudad maya bajo la selva de Guatemala.
lista.en: Mayan city discovered under the Guatemalan jungle.

lista.es: El sábado ==estoy== en la fila del banco y de repente ==se va== la luz.
lista.en: Saturday I'm in line at the bank and suddenly the power goes out.

lista.nota: Both are correct; the present is the narrative style.

lista.r: Rescatan a dos excursionistas en el Nevado de Toluca.

lista.r: Ayer voy caminando a la casa y veo un zorro.
